name: Magic Cube -> ServiceLabel accessory (10 switches + Battery, grouped)
SETUP REQUIRED after import
info:
Grouped under one accessory: a ServiceLabel node ("Magic Cube") is the parent, and all 10 switches plus Battery are linked children (isParent: false, parentService pointing at the ServiceLabel node's id). That means only ONE bridge field needs setting after import -- open the "Magic Cube" ServiceLabel node and pick your existing homekit-bridge in the "Bridge" dropdown. The 10 switches and Battery don't have a bridge field of their own; they inherit it through their parent.

These 12 nodes are also wrapped in a Node-RED canvas group ("Magic Cube (HomeKit Accessory)") purely for visual organization in the editor -- drag/move/collapse them as one unit. This is unrelated to the HomeKit-level ServiceLabel grouping above; it's just a canvas convenience and has no effect on message routing.

The flow's entry point is now the "Magic Cube: Input" link-in node, not a direct wire -- pair a "link out" (or "link call") node right after your zigbee2mqtt-in / zigbee2mqtt-get nodes, wherever they live (even a different tab), and point it at "Magic Cube: Input" by name. This whole flow then needs no wire crossing in from elsewhere, same idea as the "Magic Cube: Side" link-out below.

Each switch's ServiceLabelIndex (1-10, in the same order as the function's outputs) is what makes the Home app show them as "Magic Cube Button 1", "Magic Cube Button 2", etc. ServiceLabelNamespace on the parent is set to 1 (arabic numerals) rather than 0 (dots) for readability -- change it in the parent node's characteristicProperties if you'd rather have dots.

side (output 11) goes to a "link out" node ("Magic Cube: Side"), deliberately left outside the group and unwired to anything HomeKit-specific -- there's no single obvious HomeKit characteristic for "which face is up". Drop a "link in" node anywhere in your flow, point it at this link-out, and you're reading live side changes with no edits needed here.

name: Magic Cube -> ServiceLabel accessory (10 switches + Battery, grouped)
info:
Entry point: "Magic Cube: Input" (link in) -- pair a link-out after your zigbee2mqtt-in / zigbee2mqtt-get nodes targeting it by name, instead of wiring directly into this flow.

Each of outputs 1-10 fires only on a genuinely new gesture (fingerprint-deduped, see magic-cube-gesture-reference.md); output 12 (battery) fires on battery % change; output 11 (side) fires on resting-side change and goes to the "Magic Cube: Side" link-out placeholder described in the setup comment.
